posts.text: Old care sheets undersell it. Modern bearded dragon setups run bigger enclosures, stronger UVB, and a real basking to cool gradient you check with a temp gun.
posts.title: Bearded Dragon Setup, Updated
alt: Fully furnished bearded dragon enclosure with basking platform and UVB lighting, above a cream band reading Bearded Dragon Setup, Updated.

posts.text: A pistol shrimp snaps its claw fast enough to collapse a cavitation bubble that briefly reaches the temperature of the sun's surface, stunning prey outright.
posts.title: A Claw Hotter Than The Sun
alt: Photo of a pistol shrimp above a cream band reading A Claw Hotter Than The Sun.

posts.text: Cage type matters more than cage size for rats. A glass tank traps the ammonia buildup that drives the respiratory disease nearly every pet rat deals with.
posts.title: Never House Rats In A Tank
alt: Multi-level rat cage with ramped shelves, hammocks, a wheel, and hideouts, above a cream band reading Never House Rats In A Tank.

posts.text: The tuatara has a light sensing third eye on top of its skull, a metabolism slow enough to pass 100 years, and a lineage that predates the dinosaurs.
posts.title: The Reptile With A Third Eye
alt: Photo of a tuatara above a cream band reading The Reptile With A Third Eye.

posts.text: Discus keepers argue about gallons, but the water change routine is what actually decides the tank. Soft and slightly acidic, roughly pH 6.0 to 7.0.
posts.title: Discus: Routine Beats Tank Size
alt: Tall discus aquarium with driftwood, broadleaf plants, and visible filtration equipment, above a cream band reading Discus: Routine Beats Tank Size.

posts.text: The star-nosed mole's 22 nose tentacles carry over 25,000 sensory receptors. It finds and eats food in about 120 milliseconds, the fastest of any mammal.
posts.title: The Fastest Eater Alive
alt: Photo of a star-nosed mole above a cream band reading The Fastest Eater Alive.

posts.text: A red-footed tortoise is a tropical species, not a desert one. Humid substrate, live plants, and roughly 18 to 24 square feet of indoor floor space per adult.
posts.title: The Humid Tortoise Setup
alt: Red-footed tortoise enclosure with humid substrate, live plants, misting system, and UVB lighting, above a cream band reading The Humid Tortoise Setup.

posts.text: A threatened hagfish releases up to a liter of sticky goo in 0.1 seconds. It expands in water and clogs a predator's gills long enough for a clean escape.
posts.title: A Liter Of Slime In 0.1 Seconds
alt: Photo of a hagfish above a cream band reading A Liter Of Slime In 0.1 Seconds.

posts.text: Chinchillas bathe in dust, never water, and they overheat easily. Tall metal cage, solid shelves, a cool room, and a dust bath a few times a week.
posts.title: Chinchillas Bathe In Dust
alt: Chinchilla multi-level metal cage with solid shelves, a wheel, and a dust bath house, above a cream band reading Chinchillas Bathe In Dust.

posts.text: The bombardier beetle fires a boiling chemical spray at 100 degrees C, up to 500 pulses per second, from two chemicals it keeps stored apart until the moment it needs them.
posts.title: The Beetle That Fires Boiling Spray
alt: Photo of a bombardier beetle above a cream band reading The Beetle That Fires Boiling Spray.

posts.text: Cherry shrimp come from clear vegetated water, not open current. A planted 10 gallon tank with a gentle sponge filter gives a colony room to grow.
posts.title: The Planted Cherry Shrimp Tank
alt: A densely planted cherry shrimp aquarium with driftwood, moss, and a gentle sponge filter, above a cream band reading The Planted Cherry Shrimp Tank.

posts.text: Naked mole rats are nearly immune to cancer and can go 18 minutes without oxygen by switching their metabolism to run on fructose, the way a plant does.
posts.title: The Cancer-Proof Mammal
alt: Photo of a naked mole rat above a cream band reading The Cancer-Proof Mammal.

posts.text: Rosy boa housing stays small, dry, and simple. Most adults reach 24 to 36 inches, so a 20 gallon long with dry substrate and a hide on each side covers it.
posts.title: Rosy Boas Need It Dry
alt: Rosy boa enclosure with a dry substrate, warm and cool hides, and a secure screen lid, above a cream band reading Rosy Boas Need It Dry.

posts.text: Some sea cucumbers expel their own internal organs through their rear end to confuse a predator, then regrow a full replacement set within weeks.
posts.title: It Ejects Its Own Organs
alt: Photo of a sea cucumber on the seabed above a cream band reading It Ejects Its Own Organs.
